_readme: rules: shown on The Rules page, in order. classifier: the Classify a Food questions. Each option either points to the next question (next) or ends on a taxonomy node id (result). Adding a question here changes the classifier; no code changes needed.

rules.title: The placement key
rules.summary: Five kingdoms, checked in order. The first one that matches wins.
points: Condimenta: exists to make other food better, never the star.
Liquida: has a beverage role (hydrate, refresh, stimulate, intoxicate).
Naturalia: one food, bossed around but still recognizable.
Constructa: assembled food, where the originals can't recognize themselves or several foods share the job.
Incertae sedis: nobody can place it. Pending review, indefinitely.
rules.example: Orange juice is a single ingredient, but it is drunk, so Liquida wins before Naturalia is checked.

rules.title: The police lineup test
rules.summary: Could the original food pick the result out of a police lineup? If yes, it is Naturalia. If no, it is Constructa.
points: A cucumber can identify a pickle, so pickles are Naturalia.
Flour cannot identify toast, so toast is Constructa.
rules.example: A raisin is a grape with life experience. The grape would know.

rules.title: Role beats ingredients
rules.summary: The role a food plays at the table decides drink versus food, not whether you sip it or spoon it.
points: Food role (meal, course, snack, dessert): Constructa, even if drunk.
Beverage role (hydrate, refresh, stimulate, intoxicate): Liquida, even if assembled.
rules.example: A milkshake is a dessert wearing a straw. A cocktail is assembled, but it is still a drink.

rules.title: The container test
rules.summary: When one food holds another, the container's material decides the class. A sandwich needs a bread container (baked, griddled or fried dough) on two or more sides.
points: Bread on two sides (top and bottom): Bifaciformes, the classic.
Bread on three sides (hinged bun, split roll, fold): Trifaciformes. The hot dog lives here.
Bread on all sides, sealed: Totiformes. The burrito lives here.
Boiled or steamed dough: Dumplingae. Gyoza, ravioli, and the steamed bao.
Pressed rice: Sushiae. The California roll.
Pastry: Pieae. The pot pie.
A whole food (lettuce, banana): Pseudosandwichae. Nice try.
Bread on only one side: not a container at all. It is a topped food in Apertae.
rules.example: What is bread? Ground grain made into dough, then baked, griddled or fried. A hard taco shell is fried, so it counts. Sushi rice keeps its grains whole, so a California roll has sandwich architecture but is sushi.

rules.title: They stand or fall together
rules.summary: Foods with the same structure get the same ruling. You cannot accept one and reject the other.
points: Hot dogs and tacos share the three-sided shape. Expel one and the other goes too.
Open-faced sandwiches and thin-crust pizza share the one-sided shape. Neither is a sandwich.
rules.example: A court once ruled that one tortilla is not two slices of bread. A hot dog bun is one piece, too.

rules.title: The soup test
rules.summary: Soup is solids and liquid that were cooked together after being assembled. It may be served cold afterward.
points: Cooked together: Decocta. Soup.
Only ever combined cold: Cruda. Not soup.
Boiling water poured over noodles cooks them in place: cup noodles are soup.
rules.example: Cereal: the flakes were toasted and the milk pasteurized, but never together. Not soup. Gazpacho falls the same way, and the Board accepts the consequences.

rules.title: The vessel does not count
rules.summary: Foods are classified by how they are built, not by what they are cooked or served in.
points: A casserole is a pan, not a phylum: layered casseroles go to Stratifica, mixed ones to Mixta.
A cup of noodles is soup because of what happens inside the cup, not because of the cup.
A bread bowl is still a bowl. The chowder inside is under review.
rules.example: Lasagna and tuna noodle casserole are both baked in the same dish. One is layered, one is mixed, so they land in different phyla.

rules.title: Add-ins make varieties, not species
rules.summary: If you would still order it by its base name, an add-in creates a variety, not a new species.
points: Coffee with cream and sugar is still coffee: a variety.
A latte is ordered by a different name: a separate species.
An affogato changes role to dessert: it leaves Liquida entirely.
rules.example: A Costco hot dog is still ordered as "a hot dog," so it is a variety of Canis farcitus.

kingdom.question: What job does it do at the table?
kingdom.help: Pick the first one that fits. Order matters.

options.label: It makes other food better: a seasoning, sauce, dip or spread
You drink it to hydrate, refresh, wake up or unwind
It is one food, maybe dried, salted, pickled or grilled, but still recognizable
Several foods combined, or ingredients turned into something new
It defies explanation
Ingredients fused into one new mass (bread, pasta, sausage, cheese)
One food is the container and holds a filling
Layers or toppings on a base, with no container
Solids sitting in a liquid
Tossed together, no architecture

container.question: What is the container made of?
container.help: Bread is ground grain made into dough, then baked, griddled or fried. Fried counts.

options.label: Bread: a bun, roll, tortilla, taco shell or batter
Boiled or steamed dough: a dumpling wrapper, pasta or steamed bun
Pressed sushi rice
Pastry: pie crust or puff pastry
A whole food: lettuce, a pepper, a banana

sides.question: How many sides does the container touch the filling on?
sides.help: Look at it from the end, like a cross-section.

options.label: Two: a top and a bottom
Three: hinged, split or folded
All of them: fully sealed
One base with toppings on top
Several stacked layers

liquid.question: Were the solids and liquid cooked together after they were combined?
liquid.help: Serving it cold later is fine. What matters is whether they were ever cooked together.

options.label: Yes, cooked together
No, only ever combined cold
